commands.review_summary:
The PR changes embedded-agent orphan repair to look past non-message session metadata, branch away from the orphaned user entry, replay skipped metadata and labels, filter the repaired orphan from provider history, update the queued-user marker, and add focused regression coverage.

PR surface: Source +156, Tests +220. Total +376 across 7 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current main only checks the current session leaf for orphan repair, while the linked issue and PR proof cover the hidden-behind-metadata failure shape. I did not run a live current-main channel reproduction in this read-only review.

target.title: fix #76888: [Bug]: Queued/orphaned user-message merge can produce stale reply
target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

Fixes #76888: a channel-backed embedded-agent session left an older queued user message on the active branch and then processed a newer user prompt. The older turn stayed eligible as an active user instruction, so the model answered the stale turn and the user saw a stale visible reply.

Root cause: orphan repair only checked the current session leaf. Real runs can append non-message metadata entries such as thinking/model snapshots after the orphaned user message before prompt submission, so the actual orphaned user message was hidden behind metadata and the repair did not run.

Why does this matter now?

The issue is P1 session-state/message-loss behavior: the prompt shown to the model and the reply delivered to the user can disagree about which user turn is active. This is especially confusing in channel-backed sessions because the user only sees the final visible reply, not the queued/orphan merge state.

What is the intended outcome?

Fix classification: root-cause fix. The embedded runner now finds the trailing message entry for orphan repair by looking past non-message session metadata that does not participate in LLM context, records those skipped state-changing entries, merges the older user text as context-only prompt material, branches away from that orphan, replays the skipped state entries, and keeps the already-sanitized active session messages for the provider call.

Maintainer-ready confidence: high for the author-owned implementation and validation. The root cause is tied to the session ancestry invariant: orphan repair must inspect the message leaf even when later non-message metadata entries are the current leaf. That invariant is covered by production-runner proof, focused context-engine regression tests, the replayed-label regression, and the CI-aligned plugin SDK declaration shard. The remaining non-author decision is whether maintainers want this session-state/marker semantics over the competing candidate strategy.

What is intentionally out of scope?

Out of scope: queue semantics, Discord transport behavior, provider routing, model selection, public config/schema/protocol changes, API keys/auth, storage format migrations, and any broad rewrite of session persistence. This PR also does not change how live Discord messages are sent; it fixes the embedded-agent/session/provider boundary that decides which prompt the model should answer.

Related open PR / same-contract scan: this is an update to the existing PR for #76888, and the current daily-fix PR diagnosis resolved the linked issue to #76888 without unresolved issue references. The visible competing candidate #96533 handles a different semantic shape by dropping selected stale internal orphan prompts; this PR keeps the canonical owner boundary in the embedded runner/session repair path and preserves the old user text as context-only prompt material instead of doing downstream reply text filtering.

2026-07-01 conflict update: this branch was rebased through the main-branch conflict. The only manual conflict resolutions kept main's `wrapToolDefinition`/test `rewriteFile` additions and this PR's orphan-repair session entry/test mock additions. A fresh `check-main-drift` after the rebase reports no remaining conflicts; later main commits touch non-overlapping `message-tool`/gateway files, so daily-fix allows submit with `--allow-behind` rather than another conflict sync.

2026-07-01 commit-review follow-up: local ClawSweeper found one remaining assembled-history edge case: when a context engine appends the active prompt after history, the repaired orphan was no longer the final assembled message and could remain in provider history. This update adds a regression for that shape and removes the matching repaired orphan wherever it appears in the assembled pre-prompt history while preserving newer context-engine additions.

2026-07-02 CI/type follow-up: the latest failed required checks all surfaced the same `attempt.ts` TypeScript issue in the plugin SDK boundary declaration shard: orphan repair was using the persisted config-session `SessionEntry` type where the session-manager tree entry union was required. This update separates those two entry types, keeps quota/session-store helpers on the config-session entry type, and reruns the plugin SDK declaration shard that failed remotely.

2026-07-02 label-replay follow-up: local ClawSweeper found that replaying a label after replaying metadata kept the label pointed at the old inactive entry id. This update records old-to-new replayed entry ids and remaps label targets to the replayed metadata entry, with focused regression coverage for a label targeting a replayed model-snapshot custom entry.

What does success look like?

A provider-backed embedded run with an orphaned old user leaf plus a newer active channel prompt records `prompt:before` with the queued-context marker, the old turn, and then the latest turn; the visible reply contains the latest target and excludes the old target.

What should reviewers focus on?

Review whether the metadata-skipping rule only skips non-message entries that do not contribute LLM content, whether branching away from the orphan preserves and replays the intended trailing state changes, and whether the prompt marker wording is acceptable as the runtime contract.

## Linked context

Closes #76888

Related: ClawSweeper review on this PR requested stronger proof that the change reaches the embedded-agent/model-input boundary, not only the prompt helper.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: In a channel-backed embedded-agent run, an older orphaned queued user leaf can sit behind later session metadata and then be followed by a newer active user prompt. The fixed behavior must merge the older text as prior-turn context, remove it from the active session leaf path, and make the provider-visible answer target the later active prompt.
- Real environment tested: Production `runEmbeddedAgent` with `agent_harness=openclaw`, `messageChannel:discord`, `messageProvider:discord`, `trigger:user`, a real JSONL session seeded with a completed setup turn plus an orphaned queued user leaf, tools disabled, cache trace enabled, and a configured OpenAI-compatible provider. Provider/base URL details are redacted; no API keys or private channel identifiers are included here.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `daily_fix run-validation --name live-orphaned-user-proof-local-provider -- node --import tsx <redacted proof runner>`
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

  ```text
  Validation `live-orphaned-user-proof-local-provider` (pass, exit_code=0, 232638ms):

  [live-proof] issue 76888 orphaned queued user live proof: still running (213s)
  [agent/embedded] [trace:embedded-run] startup stages: runId=issue-76888-live-proof sessionId=issue-76888-live-proof phase=attempt-dispatch ...
  [agent/embedded] [trace:embedded-run] prep stages: runId=issue-76888-live-proof sessionId=issue-76888-live-proof phase=stream-ready ...
  [agent/embedded] Merged and removed orphaned user message to prevent consecutive user turns. runId=issue-76888-live-proof sessionId=issue-76888-live-proof trigger=user
  [live-proof] issue 76888 orphaned queued user live proof: completed (221s)
  runtime=production runEmbeddedAgent
  agent_harness=openclaw
  channel_metadata=messageChannel:discord messageProvider:discord trigger:user
  provider_model=[redacted configured OpenAI-compatible provider]
  seeded_orphan_leaf=[redacted] role=user contains=OLD_TURN_TARGET_76888
  active_prompt_contains=LATEST_TURN_TARGET_76888
  model_prompt_trace=prompt:before
  prompt_trace_count=1
  prompt_trace_match_index=0
  model_prompt_order=queued-context-marker -> OLD_TURN_76888 -> LATEST_TURN_76888
  visible_reply=LATEST_TURN_TARGET_76888
  assert_latest_target_present=true
  assert_old_target_absent=true

  payload_count=1

- Observed result after fix: The production embedded runner emitted the orphan repair log, the provider-before prompt trace contained the queued-context marker followed by the older orphaned turn and then the newer active turn, and the provider-backed visible reply was exactly `LATEST_TURN_TARGET_76888` without `OLD_TURN_TARGET_76888`.
- What was not tested: I did not send an actual Discord message through the live Discord transport, and I did not reproduce the original stochastic production stale reply end-to-end. The proof uses the production embedded runner with Discord channel metadata and a real configured provider, but the session fixture and proof runner are local and deterministic. The 2026-07-01 conflict-only update did not rerun the live provider proof; it reran focused/changed source tests after the rebase.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: Provider identity and local configuration are redacted. This proof covers the embedded-agent/session/provider boundary that decides which user turn is answered; external Discord delivery remains outside this local validation.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): The linked issue includes sanitized production evidence where `prompt.submitted` was the latest user instruction but the visible assistant output answered an earlier user message after an orphaned user-message merge.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.test.ts --project agents-embedded-agent -t "mergeOrphanedTrailingUserPrompt" --hookTimeout=300000

pnpm tsgo:prod
pnpm check:test-types
pnpm lint
bash -lc 'pnpm deadcode:dependencies && pnpm deadcode:unused-files && pnpm deadcode:report:ci:ts-unused'
```

2026-07-01 conflict-resolution validation:

```text

daily_fix run-validation --name changed-tests-after-orphan-history-filter -- node scripts/test-projects.mjs --changed origin/main
```

2026-07-02 CI/type and label-replay follow-up validation:

```text
daily_fix run-validation --name plugin-sdk-dts-after-label-remap -- node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.plugin-sdk.dts.json --declaration true
daily_fix run-validation --name label-remap-orphan-repair-focused -- pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts -t "repairs an orphaned user message behind non-message session metadata before the provider"
```

Evidence:

```text

Validation `focused-agent-tests-after-orphan-history-filter` (pass, exit_code=0, 69814ms):

```

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- Added embedded-runner/context-engine coverage for the real failure shape where a non-message session metadata leaf sits after the orphaned user message, so direct `getLeafEntry()` no longer hides the orphan from repair.
- Extended that coverage to prove state-changing entries after the orphaned user leaf are replayed in order: thinking level, model change, and a model-snapshot custom entry survive the branch/reset repair.
- Extended the metadata replay coverage again to prove labels targeting replayed metadata are retargeted to the new replayed entry id rather than left pointing at the old inactive branch entry.
- Kept the provider-seam coverage proving that the repaired prompt reaches the session/provider boundary and that the answer target remains the latest active prompt.
- Existing helper, merge strategy, and plugin SDK runtime-contract coverage continue to pin the shared queued-user marker and merge behavior.

What failed before this fix, if known?

- Before the final repair, the production live proof loaded the orphaned user message in session history but the provider-before prompt trace still contained only the latest active prompt; the orphan was hidden behind session metadata and was not merged into the repaired prompt.
- Before the state-preservation follow-up, the parent-walk repair could branch before trailing state metadata and lose persisted thinking/model/custom state. The focused regression failed until the repair collected those skipped entries and replayed them after branch/reset.
- After the first submit of the metadata repair, remote CI failed on the current PR diff because the new active-session cleanup compared `content` on the broader `AgentMessage` union and the new test mock used a narrower `(id: string)` implementation signature. The follow-up narrows both sides to user messages before reading `content` and makes the mock accept the harness' `unknown` argument shape.
- After the 2026-07-01 conflict refresh, the latest required-check failures all surfaced the same `attempt.ts` TypeScript root cause: orphan repair code used the config-session `SessionEntry` type where the session-manager tree entry union was required. The plugin SDK declaration shard now passes after the type split.
- Before the label-replay follow-up, a replayed label targeting a replayed metadata entry still used the old inactive entry id. The focused regression failed with `label:model-snapshot-leaf/model snapshot` until replay recorded old-to-new entry ids and used `label:replayed-custom/model snapshot`.
- Before the 2026-07-01 update, GitHub reported this PR as conflicting with main. The rebase conflict was in `attempt.ts` imports and `attempt.spawn-workspace.test-support.ts` mocks; both are now resolved.

If no test was added, why not?

- Tests were added.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. When an active channel prompt follows an orphaned queued user turn, the older turn is now explicitly preserved as context only and the latest active prompt remains the answer target, even if session metadata was appended after the orphan.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

What is the highest-risk area?

Embedded-runner session-state/prompt-shape compatibility for orphaned queued user repair.

How is that risk mitigated?

Patch-quality notes: the change does not drop user text, alter channel/provider routing, or change storage format. It only looks past non-message metadata entries that do not participate in LLM context, branches away from the orphaned user entry, replays the skipped state-changing entries, and keeps the already-sanitized active session messages instead of rebuilding raw transcript messages. The `return undefined` path is a defensive stop for malformed/cyclic session ancestry while walking parent entries, so the runner refuses to repair rather than guessing. The `return false` path in content comparison is also conservative: if message content cannot be serialized for an exact match, the runner does not remove any active-session message. The `unknown as Record<string, unknown>` casts are limited to optional timestamp/id comparison on already-narrowed user messages, because those fields are extension-shaped optional metadata rather than part of the discriminated content contract. The SDK runtime-contract helper touched in this PR mirrors the shared marker text for test consumers only; it is not a post-processed runtime projection and does not change raw-vs-transformed feedback boundaries. The before-feedback/source-of-truth path remains the production embedded runner repair before provider submission, not a public config/schema/protocol change.

## Current review state

What is the next action?

Maintainer-ready confidence: high for author-owned code, tests, proof, and CI-failure attribution; ready for maintainer review after CI reruns on the updated head.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?

- Author action in this update: merge conflict resolved, the assembled-history finding fixed, the remote CI type failures fixed, replayed label targets remapped, and focused/CI-aligned validations rerun.
- Local ClawSweeper commit review on `3d218c6b8a` returned ready with no blocking findings.
- CI still needs to rerun on the updated head after submit.
- RF-001: the `status: ⏳ waiting on author` label is addressed as far as author action can be before push: conflict, CI type failure, and label-remap findings are fixed locally; the visible label must refresh after submit/CI.
- RF-002/RF-008: fixed. Replayed metadata labels now remap their `targetId` through the old-to-new replayed entry id map, and focused coverage proves a label targeting the replayed model-snapshot custom entry points at the replayed id.
- RF-003: fixed for the current failed required checks. The failed logs all pointed at `attempt.ts` TypeScript errors from using the config-session `SessionEntry` type for session-manager tree entries; the type split is in this branch and the plugin SDK declaration shard now passes locally.
- RF-004: disclosed as maintainer-owned session-state compatibility. The author-side guardrails are focused tests, production-runner proof, state replay, label target remap, and explicit out-of-scope boundaries; final acceptance of the ancestry rewrite semantics remains with maintainers.
- RF-005: disclosed as maintainer-owned marker wording compatibility. The shared marker remains pinned by runtime and SDK contract coverage, but exact provider-visible wording is still a maintainer decision.
- RF-006: disclosed as maintainer-owned competing-fix choice. #96533 has different stale-prompt semantics, while this PR preserves the old turn as context-only material and keeps the latest active prompt as the answer target.
- RF-007: fixed for the narrow author-action item. The replayed-label remap was implemented with focused regression coverage; the broader session-state strategy choice remains maintainer-owned.
- RF-009: covered by focused orphan-repair validation in the context-engine test file after the label-remap update.
- RF-010: the previously recorded full `pnpm tsgo:prod` validation remains in the PR evidence; for the latest remote CI failure root cause, the CI-aligned plugin SDK declaration shard was rerun and passed after the type split.
- RF-011: the previously recorded full `pnpm check:test-types` validation remains in the PR evidence; the latest focused test/type follow-up does not change test-only type surfaces outside the touched orphan-repair tests.
- RF-012: the previously recorded full `pnpm lint` validation remains in the PR evidence; the latest changes are typed helper/test updates and local ClawSweeper review passed after the label-remap follow-up.
- A live Discord transport replay was not run; local validation covers the production embedded-runner/session/provider boundary with Discord channel metadata.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?

- Conflict status / RF-001: addressed by rebasing through main and resolving the import/test-support mock conflicts.
- Local ClawSweeper assembled-history finding: addressed with a failing-then-passing regression where a context engine appends the active prompt after history, plus a runtime cleanup that removes the matching repaired orphan while preserving newer assembled messages.
- Remote CI / RF-003: addressed by separating config-session entries from session-manager tree entries and rerunning the plugin SDK declaration shard that failed in CI.
- Label replay / RF-002/RF-008: addressed by recording replayed entry id mappings and retargeting labels to replayed metadata entries, with focused regression coverage.
- RF-004/RF-005/RF-006/RF-007: disclosed as maintainer-owned compatibility/strategy decisions after author-side code, proof, and focused guardrails were updated.
- RF-009/RF-010/RF-011/RF-012: validation status is recorded above; the latest focused and CI-aligned follow-up checks passed, and earlier full type/lint/build lanes remain listed in the validation evidence.
